result.title: Learning momenta for Hamiltonian-based models
result.summary: There has been increasing interest in methodologies that incorporate physics priors into neural network architectures to enhance their modeling capabilities. Among these methodologies, Hamiltonian neural networks (HNNs) and their variants have gained considerable attention. These architectures explicitly encode Hamiltonian mechanics both in their structure and loss function, resulting in desirable properties and additional modeled information. A crucial limitation of HNNs is their reliance on data on the target system's generalized momenta. This severely hampers their applicability when the analytical form of the generalized momenta is unknown, which frequently is the case in real-world applications. The goal of the present work is to develop a general extension of Hamiltonian-based architectures that addresses this issue by simultaneously learning the system's generalized momenta, Hamiltonian structure, and dynamics from data. The proposed architecture learns the generalized momenta when their analytical form is unknown, and only (potentially non-sequential) data on the state and its derivatives is available. A dissipative mass-spring system, a double pendulum, and a rolling disk under nonholonomic constraints are considered as canonical examples to assess the performance of the proposed architecture.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一种 Hamiltonian 神经网络的推广：在广义动量解析形式未知时，仅用状态及其导数的（可不按时间顺序的）数据同时学习广义动量、Hamiltonian 结构与动力学，并在耗散质量-弹簧系统、双摆和非完整约束滚盘上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其从可观测数据中恢复不可观测内部状态并与结构化动力学联合训练的做法，可能与 LVR 中 latent 状态的结构约束、可辨识性与监督分配问题存在概念类比，可供核查。
